title: single application
statement: Oracyl is one Android app adapting phone and DeX; it is not two separate user products.

title: command center
statement: Give Operator one consistent interface to Victor chat, research, tasks, apps, tabs, projects, skills, accounts, library and settings.

title: aesthetic canon
statement: Operator controls layout, brand and style. Victor implements the approved appearance and must not silently redesign it.

title: no kernel action
statement: UI specification does not authorize any change to Victor core kernel, platform privileges, accounts, or autonomous external permissions.

title: Oracyl versus Victor
statement: Oracyl names the app; Victor names the AI/system engaged from that app; do not carry over ChatGPT branding.

title: Chats
statement: Chats is top-level navigation position 1 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Chats intent
statement: Converse directly with Victor and resume saved threads without losing context.

title: Research
statement: Research is top-level navigation position 2 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Research intent
statement: Run, inspect, continue, and retrieve Victor research work, with findings, sources, and status preserved.

title: Tasks
statement: Tasks is top-level navigation position 3 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Tasks intent
statement: Create, monitor, review, and manage scheduled or bounded work.

title: Apps
statement: Apps is top-level navigation position 4 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Apps intent
statement: Launch purposeful applications hosted within Oracyl without leaving the primary workspace.

title: Tabs
statement: Tabs is top-level navigation position 5 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Tabs intent
statement: Reopen browser pages or in-app content tabs; maintain a Chromium-like optional browsing workspace inside Oracyl.

title: Projects
statement: Projects is top-level navigation position 6 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Projects intent
statement: Organize work into persistent project workspaces with relevant conversations, files, research, and tasks.

title: Skills
statement: Skills is top-level navigation position 7 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Skills intent
statement: Discover, review, and invoke Victor capabilities/skills without conflating them with hosted Apps.

title: Accounts
statement: Accounts is top-level navigation position 8 of 8. Dropdown expansion retains order.

title: Accounts intent
statement: Connect, view, and manage identities/integrations and the permissions attached to them.

title: Pinned mixed types
statement: Pinned contains cross-resource shortcuts to chats, tasks, research, projects, browser tabs, apps or skills; do not clone source content.

title: Recents distinct
statement: Recent Chats is a recency ordered list of chats, separate from mixed-type Pinned.

title: Footer
statement: Library and Settings are visually grouped in an anchored bottom navigation/footer area.

title: Desktop reference
statement: The desktop visual gold state is 1920x1080 CSS px; sidebar 335px and upper tab strip 52px at that viewport.

title: Phone reference
statement: Phone baseline is 360x780 CSS px at device scale factor 2 (PNG 720x1560).

title: Desktop sidebar
statement: DeX/desktop shows persistent ordered sidebar, Pinned and Recent sections, and footer.

title: Phone drawer
statement: Phone shows hamburger-operated overlay drawer, scrim dismissal, and same navigation hierarchy.

title: Phone settings
statement: Phone settings uses full-screen back navigation and grouped charcoal cards; rows may initially be placeholders.

title: System chrome
statement: On Android, real system status and navigation bars come from OS, never duplicate them in the native host.

title: Fixed first tab
statement: Oracyl is the leftmost fixed non-closable primary tab.

title: Secondary tab close
statement: Only secondary tabs carry close X; Oracyl itself has no X.

title: Secondary checkmark
statement: ✓ next to X saves a browser tab under the Tabs category; this is separate from mixed-type pinned shortcut.

title: No browser wrapper
statement: Optional browser capability is inside Oracyl; no URL bar/bookmarks/extension chrome wrapped around Oracyl.

title: Canonical logo
statement: Use same SVG everywhere: dot above, comma below inside purple/near-black yin-yang; not a two-dot standard yin-yang.

title: Dark only
statement: The canonical app interface is dark on both phone and DeX.

title: Composer
statement: Keep message input reachable at bottom. When text is present the voice control may change to Send.

title: Phone interaction
statement: Phone chat supports user bubble, assistant body, copy/reaction/speaker/share controls and top toolbar.

title: Real transport
statement: Actual chat messages must connect to Victor and display honest pending/error/success states; local echo is not completion.

title: One data source
statement: Both phone and DeX draw from same resources by stable IDs and preserve pins/drafts/selection across transitions.

title: Groups
statement: Settings has four groups: identity/connections; personalization; general; privacy/about.

title: Consent
statement: No account integration, credential grant, or external action without user-controlled permissions.

title: Sandbox
statement: Untrusted websites cannot access privileged Victor native bridge automatically.

title: Preview honesty
statement: Prototype is offline HTML demo; not an APK nor full live backend.

title: Unimplemented real features
statement: Browser engine, accounts, persistence, scheduler, app runtime and speech capture are not shipped in preview.

title: No copied identities
